Subject: Recap: Performance SLOs & context window (FinCo discovery)

Hi Sarah / Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned:

Key requirements we captured:
- Context window: up to ~12k tokens of user documents (legal + contract history) per request as input.
- Output: extractive/abstractive summary up to ~2k tokens max.
- Latency SLO: target perceived latency p95 <= 1s for the full response; preference for streaming for outputs > 512 tokens to improve perceived latency.
- Concurrency/throughput: peak concurrent sessions ~50, average ~200 reqs/min, with bursts up to ~80 rps.
- Streaming: need chunked streaming with <200ms chunk arrival target for interactive UX.

Open questions / asks from our side:
1) Can you share a few representative prompt + document examples (we can treat these as test payloads for benchmarking)?
2) Which use-cases are most latency-sensitive vs. batchable (e.g., summary for UI vs. nightly bulk processing)?
3) Any constraints around model footprint / quantization or specific hardware (e.g., customer requires CPU-only or on-prem GPU)?

Next steps we propose:
- You provide sample payloads and a short list of priority flows (Sarah/Alex).
- Redwood will run a scoped performance benchmark (2 weeks) using your samples and share p50/p95 numbers across candidate model variants and streaming configs.

Attachments: FinCo_scoping_notes.docx, redwood_perf_baseline.csv (initial notes + baseline metrics).

I’ll loop in Rishi and Vivek to coordinate the benchmark and logistics.

Thanks,

Thanks for the quick confirmation and for offering the sample payloads, Sarah. A few notes from the Redwood engineering side on how the context window + max tokens interact with latency and what we’ll test in the benchmark: 

Technical notes (high level):
- Attention & KV cache effects: longer input contexts and larger KV caches increase memory pressure and per-token compute. For decoder-only models this typically increases per-token generation latency roughly linearly with context length for KV lookups; the exact delta depends on model architecture and kernel optimizations.
- Streaming vs full-generation: streaming (token-by-token / chunked) reduces perceived latency for users because partial results arrive before the full generation completes. For very long outputs we recommend streaming + small initial chunk size (e.g., 64–128 tokens) to hit the <200ms perceived chunk target in typical infra.
- Batch sizing tradeoffs: batching increases throughput and cost-efficiency but can add queueing latency. For your interactive SLOs we’ll primarily prioritize small batch sizes (1–8) and use dynamic batching for background/batch flows.
- Mitigations we’ll evaluate: prefix caching for repeated documents, retrieval + condensed context (RAG with condensed prompts), model quantization profiles (4-bit) to reduce memory pressure, and routing to lower-latency variants for interactive flows.

Estimated ballpark latency impacts (empirical targets we’ll validate in the PoC):
- 512-token input + 256-token output: p95 ~200–450ms (depending on model variant and hardware).
- 12k-token input + 2k-token output (no streaming): p95 can be multiple seconds on a single-shot generation; with streaming and chunked decoding we expect the first chunks to arrive within ~300–700ms and the tail to finish later — we’ll quantify this precisely in the benchmark.

What we need from you for the scoped benchmark:
- 3 sample payloads (short/medium/long) + expected client-side UX (e.g., want first chunk by X ms).
- A list of priority flows (interactive vs. batch) so we can set batching policy and model selection accordingly.

Next steps / timeline:
1) You share payloads by EOD Wed (thanks!).
2) Redwood runs a 2-week scoped perf run across 2–3 model variants and streaming configs. Deliverables: p50/p95 latency matrix, throughput under target concurrency, and recommendations (truncation/stream config, batching, quantization).
3) Joint review & decision on reserved vs hosted capacity.

I’ve attached our perf_benchmark_plan.pdf with the test matrix we’ll run. Rishi/Vivek/Laura — can you confirm infra availability to kick off once we receive samples?

Thanks,
Marissa
